Subject: Rowan Financial - prioritized activation asks & timeline

Team — quick one. Rowan (large enterprise banking client) verbally committed yesterday contingent on two prioritized items in our activation plan: 1) a soft residency guarantee for a defined model family for the first 90 days (they want predictable latency), and 2) exportable per-tenant audit logs (they have an upcoming audit and need evidence).

High-level ask: can we get an internal decision on whether we can (a) reserve a warm pool / soft residency policy for their account (no strict SLA, but higher probability of kept model residency), and (b) ship an exportable audit log bundle (JSON/CSV) for tenant usage and traces within 3–4 weeks?

Why this matters: procurement wants the commitment in the SOW to close this quarter (deal id ROW-2026-1196). If we can't commit a residency mitigation and the audit export, they will push for a longer SOC validation window and likely delay signature beyond their Q4 close. Alex (cc) can provide the procurement language.

Attachments: ROWAN_SOW_v3.pdf (proposed SOW), activation-map.xlsx (high-level timeline).

What I need: a short feasibility note from Product/Eng with suggested scope and any non-negotiable blockers by EOD PST. If we can do this, I will shepherd the commercial commitment.

—Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz | Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Rowan Financial - prioritized activation asks & timeline

Thanks for the clear ask, Vanessa — appreciate the context. Quick responses while I sync with Eng:

- Residency: we have two levers here — a reserved warm pool (Dedicated-style reservation) or a routing preference (soft affinity). A true SLA-backed residency requires capacity reservation and billing implications; soft affinity is lower-risk and could be done more quickly but provides less hard guarantee.

- Audit export: we have an existing export pipeline for per-tenant billing traces (internal alpha) — we need to confirm retention windows and whether it includes the full request/response payloads or only metadata. Building a configurable export bundle (JSON) is doable, but depends on whether Rowan needs signed chain-of-custody for audit.

I will ask Jonas for a technical breakdown (effort and time) and Priyom for recommended customer-facing wording for the SOW. If we can get an engineering estimate by noon PST I can draft SOW language to match.

Irene Choi | Dir., Product Management — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Rowan Financial - prioritized activation asks & timeline

Short technical readout from Eng:

1) Soft residency (routing preference): low cost. We can implement tenant-level affinity using existing routing tags and a sticky-weighted policy. Timeline: ~3 business days to configure policy + 1 day for validation in staging. No infra changes. Caveats: not a hard guarantee — during peak usage we could still evict model residency.

2) Warm pool / reserved capacity (semi-hard residency): requires reserving capacity in our Dedicated pool or creating a soft-reserve fallback in hosted. If the ask is for a 90-day residency with high probability, we'd need to provision a reserved stand-by instance or a quota carve-out. Impact: capacity commit, cost to Rowan or to Redwood (commercial negotiation). Implementation timeline: ~2–3 weeks for capacity allocation, testing, and activation assuming infra availability.

3) Audit export: we have an endpoint that can stream per-request metadata to S3; however, full request/response export with PII redaction hooks is not yet a polished product feature. Engineering estimate to produce a vetted export bundle (JSON + checksums, retention config, and a simple download UI) is ~10–12 business days, plus security review (SOC evidence) that could add another week. If Rowan is amenable to a limited initial bundle (metadata + traces without full user payloads), we could accelerate to ~5 business days.

Blocking questions for Vanessa/Rowan:
- Do they require full request bodies in the audit bundle or is metadata sufficient for their auditor?
- Are they willing to accept a commercial carve-out (monthly fee) to cover reserved capacity?

I recommend two options to present to Rowan: Option A (fast): soft affinity + accelerated metadata-only export (5 business days). Option B (commit): reserved capacity + full audit bundle (3–4 weeks + procurement).

—Jonas
Jonas Weber | Eng. Lead, Serving Runtime

Thanks Jonas — this is helpful and clean. Answers to your blockers from Rowan (Alex):
- Auditor only requires request/response headers and full model output. They do not require raw customer prompt bodies to be included in the export; redacted prompt bodies are acceptable.
- They are open to a commercial carve-out for reserved capacity if we can provide a clear monthly charge and a 90-day commitment window. Procurement (cc) expects SOW language and an estimate for the carve-out fee by next Tuesday.

Priyom — can you draft conservative SOW wording (Option A and Option B) that aligns with Jonas's technical options? For Option B, include the carve-out as a line item and an acceptance criteria set for the audit bundle (fields included, retention period).

I'll update Alex and loop legal once we have SOW language. We need a decision path: preferred is Option B (reserved capacity + full audit bundle) but we'd accept Option A to accelerate signature this week if eng can hit the 5 business day export turnaround.

—Vanessa

Attachment referenced: ROWAN_SOW_v3.pdf (proposed language reflecting negotiated commercial points).

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Rowan Financial - prioritized activation asks & timeline

Attached a first-pass SOW snippet (see activation-map.xlsx) and two clean options for commercial copy:

- Option A (accelerate): Soft affinity routing + metadata-only audit export. Delivery: export delivery pipeline enabled and validated in staging within 5 business days of agreement. Acceptance: downloadable JSON with request metadata and model outputs. No dedicated capacity.

- Option B (commit): 90-day reserved capacity carve-out (monthly carve-out fee TBD) + full audit export with redacted prompts, model outputs, trace checksums, and one-time SOC-style evidence package. Delivery: 3–4 weeks for provisioning + security review. Acceptance: downloadable bundle + signed confirmation of export integrity.

I'm flagging a borderline item: billing and chargeback for reserved capacity needs finance alignment — we will include a placeholder fee in the SOW and then finalize after capacity assessment.

Next steps I propose: 1) Present Options A/B to Rowan with recommended commercial placeholders (Vanessa); 2) If Rowan selects A, Eng (Jonas) to spin up metadata export pipeline and test within 5 business days; 3) If Rowan selects B, Eng + Infra to provision reserved pool and Legal/Finance to finalize carve-out terms.

—Priyom Das
Solutions Engineering
